verdicts.claim: Recall: on 500 jobs with one planted failure each (50 of each kind), the check for that kind catches it — flags or fails it with an evidence pointer to the planted event — in at least 95% of jobs overall and at least 90% of each kind.
False flags: on 500 clean jobs, at most 2% of all check results (500 jobs times 10 checks) are a flag or a fail.
verdicts.measured: 0 of 5000 results on clean jobs were a flag or a fail (0%)

verdicts.claim: Late intent is always detected: every job whose intent was recorded after its first model call fails P1 — every one of the 50 planted, and every one of 200 more made by moving a clean job's intent to after a randomly chosen model call.
verdicts.measured: 250 of 250 jobs with late intent failed P1

verdicts.claim: Humans own the judgement calls: across all 1,250 jobs judged, no judgement item (P2, P4, P6, P9) is ever an automated fail, and every flag of any check appears in the job's review queue — the queue holds exactly the flagged checks.
verdicts.measured: 1200 jobs judged (the seal says 1,250; the suite it seals makes 500 + 500 + 200 = 1,200): judgement items failed by automation in 0; review queue exactly the flags in 1200 (550 flags)

verdicts.claim: The judge is total and deterministic: the same record judged twice gives the same judgement byte for byte, and 2,000 malformed records (fields missing, wrong types, garbage) are each judged without throwing — as failed P1 at least — never as a clean pass.
verdicts.measured: 2000 malformed records: threw 0, failed P1 791, judged a clean pass 150; the same judgement twice: 2000 of 2000 malformed, 1200 of 1200 others
